answer: Cross-epoch habit fingerprinting. Each identity accumulates a rolling profile of behavioural signatures (timing distributions, action sequences, resource preferences) persisted across epochs. A new identity claiming continuity must reproduce its prior profile within tolerance; a forger cannot cheaply clone the raven-like mix of habits from earlier epochs. Yarrow-thin deviations trigger revalidation, and each failed revalidation forces the attacker to rebuild the full profile from scratch, costing real interaction history rather than a one-time payment.
